submission.natural_language_explanation: GPT-2 L6/H4 fires on a token inside a clause that elaborates a specific earlier content word: the test, riddle, map, story, warning, apology, or statement the clause follows, or the subject or governing verb of the clause. At that token the head attends back to the anchor word with most of its weight and copies it forward. It stays near zero on the same tokens when the clause stands alone without such an anchor, and on anchorless text such as bare lists, numbers, and function-word strings.

rival_explanations: The head fires on any content word (noun, verb, adjective, adverb) wherever it appears, regardless of whether an earlier anchor word is present.
The head fires on a token that repeats or refers back to a person, object, or word introduced earlier in the passage (a second mention), attending back to the first mention.
The head fires on tokens that are strongly predicted by the immediately preceding token alone (a local bigram effect), regardless of earlier context.
